minutes.headline: Commission voted to keep firearm hunting off two more properties and allow firearm possession, effective July 1.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting went to amending the draft land use regulations after heated public comment on hunting and firearms. The commission also heard several wetlands hearings and continued a contested new-house application at Fire Road 16 to May 19. It handled enforcement items and two small payments.

public_comment.topic: Commissioner Bursch described an online personal attack and threat to his business after the March 3 meeting.
Commissioner Luck rebutted remarks about his availability at the April 21 meeting.
Opposed the proposed hunting and firearm regulation changes and criticised the chair's words and vote.
Rebutted the prior speaker on crossbow hunting, buffer zones and Hunting Hills.
Closing comment thanking the board and noting the high public participation.

decisions.decision: Applicants for 238 Fire Road 16 will return with revised plans: remove or reduce retaining walls, move the stockpile, supply a waiver request, a turtle letter and a catch basin maintenance plan.
Effective date of the new land use rules set at July 1 to allow signage and notice.
The administrator will invite the 48 Oak Ridge Road owners to the next meeting instead of issuing an immediate enforcement order.
Fire Road 12 notice of intent to be re-advertised for the June 2 meeting.
Review of the Reynolds Hollis cutting plan set for the second June meeting.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to amend the draft land use rules so firearm hunting is not expanded, and rejected a ban on possessing firearms on conservation land.
A motion to table the land use regulation changes for 90 days failed.
The commission adopted the rules as amended, with an effective date of July 1 to allow signage and notice.
The contested new-house hearing at 238 Fire Road 16 was continued to May 19, with revised plans, a waiver request, a turtle letter and a catch basin plan to come.
On enforcement at 48 Oak Ridge Road, the administrator will invite the owners to the next meeting; an enforcement order was moved and later withdrawn.

why_it_matters: The amended rules set what is allowed on town conservation land, including hunting and firearms, and they take effect July 1, so anyone who walks, hunts or uses those properties will be working under the new rules.
The Fire Road 16 house application is still open, so abutters and residents have another chance to weigh in at the May 19 hearing.
watch_next: May 19: continued hearings for 238 Fire Road 16, 137 Flynn Road and 757 Chase Road.
July 1: effective date of the amended land use regulations; June 2: re-advertised Fire Road 12 notice of intent.
